subject: Clarify where customer requests are processed, subprocessor list, and cross-border controls
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@nexahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Eva Morales <eva.morales@nexahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q on where requests are processed + subprocessors

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — NexaHealth is excited about Redwood's latency and the analytics surface. Before we loop legal, two quick questions to confirm for our security review:

1) Where are API requests from EU users actually processed (region granularity)? Do requests stay in the EU or cross to the US for model execution?
2) If requests leave the EU, what mechanisms (SCCs, encryption, KMS) and subprocessors are involved in those cross-border paths?
3) What's the deletion SLA for request payloads and any derived artifacts (embeddings, logs)?

We need concise answers we can include in our procurement pack. If it's easier to share a short diagram or inventory, that would be great.

Appreciate it — Sam

--
Sam Patel
Director, Product Security
NexaHealth
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Eva Morales <eva.morales@nexahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests are processed + subprocessors

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa from our security/compliance team; she can provide the evidence and the subprocessor inventory.

Quick summary to start:
- For hosted API customers, we perform request routing by region. EU-region requests are routed to compute in our EU cloud region by default.
- Certain model variants (particularly some community/open checkpoints we host) may only be available in our US compute pools. When a requested model variant is not available in-region, the request will be routed to the nearest compatible pool (documented fallback).
- Cross-border transfer controls: we use contractual safeguards (SCCs) and TLS in transit; data at rest is encrypted with customer keys where configured (KMS). We can provide the signed SCC text and KMS configuration examples.
- Deletion: request payloads are kept transiently by default (30 days for logs/observability artifacts; request-level content retention is 0–7 days depending on customer plan). Embeddings/derived artifacts retention depends on the feature and is configurable; we offer full purge on request + verification evidence for enterprise contracts.

I'm attaching a simple processing footprint diagram and the latest subprocessor CSV — Marissa, can you expand the answers and share the evidence links (SCC, SOC2 section, deletion verification process)?

Best,
Jordan

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@nexahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Eva Morales <eva.morales@nexahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where requests are processed + subprocessors

Hi Sam — thanks for the questions. Below is a concise Q&A + evidence pointers you can paste into procurement. I've kept answers targeted to the EU-scenario you outlined. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the diagram.

Q1: Where are API requests from EU users processed?
- Hosted (self-managed routing): EU requests are routed to our EU compute region (Frankfurt / eu-central-1) by default. This includes request handling, tokenization, and model execution for models we host in-region.
- Fallbacks: If a requested model variant isn't available in-region (common for some third-party/open models or preview variants), Redwood will route execution to the nearest compatible region (typically US-east). The routing policy is transparent in our Console and can be pinned per-customer.

Q2: If requests leave the EU, what mechanisms and subprocessors are involved?
- Legal/contractual: We execute EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) with customers for cross-border data processing where applicable. We also offer Data Processing Addendums that enumerate transfer mechanisms.
- Encryption & key control: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+). At rest, customer data is encrypted with our platform keys by default. For Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM (example: AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault).
- Subprocessors: Primary subprocessors in the cross-border path include cloud compute providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) and a managed logging provider (LogStream Inc.). The attached CSV lists the current inventory and processing locations per subprocessors. Note: some small analytics/observability vendors operate US-based services for metrics aggregation.

Q3: Deletion SLA for request payloads and derived artifacts
- Hosted default policy: request payloads are not persisted beyond necessary runtime; transient request logs are retained for up to 30 days for debugging/monitoring.
- Embeddings & derived vectors: retention is configurable. Default hosted retention is 90 days unless the customer opts into longer retention.
- Enterprise options: for Dedicated/Private customers we support immediate purge (same-day) and provide a signed deletion certificate and proof-of-deletion (audit log entries). For hosted customers we can negotiate shorter retention and a verified purge workflow as part of contract negotiations.

Evidence & artifacts (links):
- Subprocessor inventory (attached): subprocessor_inventory_redwood_20261029.csv
- Processing footprint diagram (attached): redwood_residency_diagram_v1.png
- SCC template & DPA excerpt: https://drive.google.com/file/d/SCCTemplateExample
- SOC 2 summary & cert: https://drive.google.com/file/d/SOC2ReportSummary
- Deletion verification process: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cEvidenceLink

Operational controls to call out:
- Customer can pin models & region routing at the account level to avoid cross-border routing for hosted API.
- We offer Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments if NexaHealth requires zero cross-border processing.
- Audit logs include request routing decisions, region, and subprocessors used; logs can be retained in-region for customers on the enterprise plan.

If you want, I'll also export the minimal set of artifacts Nexa legal typically requests (SCC, subprocessor list, SOC 2 excerpts, deletion certificate template).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

1) Can you confirm whether the logging provider (LogStream Inc.) ever receives unredacted request text for debugging? If so, is that limited to US-based environments only?
2) Please add a one-line statement we can include in our procurement brief: "Redwood does / does not route production requests outside of the EU for customers who pin EU-region routing."

If you can drop both items into that Drive folder you linked, we'll be able to move to legal review. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Sam
